## Fixes

- **`rclone mount` of an s3 remote with `provider = KamPlexFS` no
  longer drops files from the VFS cache as changed on the server.**
  With a server which stores sub-second modification times, a file
  just uploaded, moved, copied or read with a HEAD request reported
  its modification time with nanoseconds, but the same file from a
  listing reported whole seconds. The VFS cache took the difference
  as a change on the server and dropped the cached file, about half
  of all uploads in a 24 hour mount test. Dropping a file which was
  still in use could make reads return zeros, or a truncate or
  overwrite store a file with the wrong size. Those races are in
  upstream rclone's VFS cache, which now only meets them as often as
  official rclone does. The s3 backend now
  reports the modification time at the 1 second precision of the
  listings whatever it was read from, unless
  `kamplexfs_exact_modtime = true`, which is unchanged. The
  `kamplexfs` backend didn't have this problem.
